item: a mailbox pull on a plain port upgrades with STARTTLS before any credential, or is refused
key_paths: src/ingest/email.py; src/api/ingestion.py; tests/test_mailbox_starttls_r651.py; tests/test_mailbox_stall_r647.py; tests/test_mailbox_stop_r640.py; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/USER_MANUAL.md
summary: use_ssl=false (accepted by both mailbox API routes, never sent by the UI) ran IMAP/POP3 in plaintext, LOGIN/USER/PASS included. It now upgrades with STARTTLS (IMAP) or STLS (POP3) before any credential, with the same verifying context as a TLS port (R650), the upgraded socket registered for the Stop before its handshake (R647) and the switch read before each command; a server that does not offer the upgrade, refuses it, or fails the certificate check is refused with a sentence naming the server, the port and the cause, with no fallback. Any other TLS failure on either path (a plain server on a TLS port, an old protocol only) is now refused the same way instead of surfacing as OpenSSL's raw text, and the direct route answers every such refusal as a 502. The mailbox disclosure says the password is never sent unencrypted. Release line: a newsletter mailbox pull never sends your password unencrypted: on a plain port it first switches to an encrypted, certificate-checked connection (STARTTLS) and is refused, saying why, if the server cannot.
